paragraph: In the image channel the framework score separated nuisance variation from errors of severity ≥ 0.2 with AUC = 0.914 ([0.887, 0.938]), compared with 0.919 for PSNR and 0.769 for unweighted SSIM; the strongest single baseline was Edge F1 (AUC = 0.934). The score decreased monotonically with severity for 8 of 9 error families (median Spearman ρ = -0.89). The mesh channel was invariant to rigid rotation, uniform scaling, re-triangulation and micro-noise (mean score 100.0, minimum 100.0; mean Chamfer distance 0.009 versus 0.248 without pose alignment). Against nuisance variation the framework reached AUC = 0.971 for geometric errors, versus 0.541 for Chamfer distance without alignment. For render-level errors in six Blender compositions, standardised re-rendering raised the framework's AUC from 0.749 (screenshots from jittered viewpoints) to 0.985; correct scenes scored 97.4 on average when re-rendered with different sample counts and resolutions, but 43.8 as viewpoint-jittered screenshots. Re-rendering was deterministic (maximum pixel difference 0, identical mesh export: True). Screenshots that contained the application interface scored 0.0 on average and 100.0 after automatic viewport cropping; an auxiliary floor reduced the mesh score to 74.4 without and 100.0 with helper-component removal. Mean assessment time was 0.07 s per image and 0.07 s per mesh on a CPU; one Blender re-render took 1.03 s.
